title: Exception Handling
intro: Learn the basic ideas of Exception Handling in simple English. Read the explanation and example first; the quiz asks only from the concepts taught here.

items.heading: Exception
items.text: An exception is an event raised when something goes wrong while a program is running.

items.heading: try
items.text: Code that may raise an exception is placed in a try block.

items.heading: except
items.text: except handles an exception raised by the try block.

items.heading: Specific exceptions
items.text: Catching a specific exception is clearer and safer than catching everything blindly.

items.heading: else
items.text: The else block runs when the try block finishes without an exception.

items.heading: finally
items.text: finally runs whether an exception occurred or not, so it is useful for cleanup.

items.heading: raise
items.text: raise lets your code deliberately create an exception when a condition is invalid.

items.heading: Built-in exceptions
items.text: Python provides common exception types such as ValueError, TypeError, KeyError and FileNotFoundError.

items.heading: Multiple except blocks
items.text: A try block may have multiple except blocks to handle different exception types differently.

items.heading: Do not hide errors
items.text: Silently ignoring every exception can hide real bugs. Handle errors meaningfully or let unexpected errors surface.
